# Local-First Docker Mode Spec

**Status:** DRAFT
**Author:** Hubify Labs (auto-generated by the build readiness loop, K7)
**Date:** 2026-04-09
**Linked from:** PRD §9 · `feedback_feynman_competitor.md` · BUILD_READINESS_CHECKLIST K7
**Companion docs:** `DEPLOYMENT_INFRA_PLAN.md` (the canonical Fly.io path) · `DESKTOP_APP_SPEC.md`

---

## 0. Why this mode exists

The default Hubify Labs deployment is the always-on Fly.io orchestrator described in PRD §9 + DEPLOYMENT_INFRA_PLAN §2.3. That model is right for most users — it runs 24/7, it survives laptop sleep, and it's the only way to get true cron-driven autonomous loops.

But three classes of users need a different model:

1. **Privacy-sensitive researchers** — bio + clinical labs touching gated data (UK Biobank · MIMIC-IV · ADNI · TCGA), national-security-adjacent astronomy (export-controlled mission data), and any researcher whose IRB or contract forbids data leaving their machine.
2. **Air-gapped environments** — research stations on ships, remote field sites, or institutional networks that block outbound traffic to anything that isn't an academic mirror.
3. **Cost-conscious solo users** — students or hobbyists who already pay for a beefy desktop and don't want a second monthly bill.

For these users, Feynman's local-only model is a feature we currently don't match. **Local Docker mode** closes that gap. The user runs `hubify lab create my-lab --local` and the orchestrator boots in a local Docker container instead of a Fly.io machine. Everything else stays the same: same web UI, same desktop app, same CLI, same agents.

**The tradeoff** is documented up front in §6 below: local mode loses always-on, public lab sites, cross-lab comms, and ntfy phone push. The spec is designed to make these tradeoffs visible, not invisible.

---

## 1. What "local-first" means here

Local-first Docker mode is **a deployment topology**, not a separate product. The bits that change:

| Layer | Default (Fly.io) | Local Docker mode |
|---|---|---|
| **Orchestrator host** | Fly.io shared-cpu machine, ~$2-5/lab/month | Local Docker container on the user's macOS / Linux box |
| **Convex backend** | Hosted Convex (cloud) | **Optional:** can stay on hosted Convex OR run a local SQLite shim (privacy-strict mode) |
| **Vercel public site** | `<lab>.hubify.app` auto-deployed | **Disabled** — no public site is generated |
| **Cross-lab comms** | Comm gateway via Fly machines | **Disabled** — local labs cannot read or send comms with cloud labs |
| **Backups** | Backblaze B2 nightly + GitHub LFS | **User-configurable:** can stay on B2 (encrypted client-side) OR write to a local external drive |
| **RunPod GPU** | Same — RunPod is always external | Same — local Docker mode does NOT change GPU access · users still rent RunPod pods |
| **Web UI** | Hosted at `app.hubify-labs.com` | Same hosted UI · OR run locally on `localhost:3000` if Convex is also local |
| **Desktop app** | Connects to Fly orchestrator | Connects to local Docker orchestrator on `localhost:8080` |
| **CLI** | `hubify` binary talks to Fly | Same `hubify` binary · `--profile local` switches the endpoint |
| **MCP server** | Stdio + SSE + WebSocket | Same · all 3 transports work locally |
| **24/7 cron** | **Yes** — Fly machine never sleeps | **No** — orchestrator only runs when the user's machine is awake. Cron jobs queue and fire on next boot. |

The principle: **same surface contract, different host.** A user can switch between local and cloud mode by changing one CLI flag and a few env vars. Labs are not locked to one mode.

---

## 2. Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  User's macOS / Linux machine                                   │
│                                                                 │
│  ┌─────────────┐     ┌──────────────────────────────────┐       │
│  │ Desktop App │     │ Docker container: hubify-orch    │       │
│  │ (Tauri 2)   │◄───►│   ├ Node.js orchestrator         │       │
│  └─────────────┘     │   ├ Convex local shim (sqlite)   │       │
│                      │   ├ Agent runtime (Claude Code)  │       │
│  ┌─────────────┐     │   ├ MCP server (3 transports)    │       │
│  │ CLI binary  │◄───►│   └ HTTP API on :8080            │       │
│  └─────────────┘     └──────────────────────────────────┘       │
│                                ▲                                 │
│                                │ (volumes)                       │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────┐         │
│  │ ~/.hubify/labs/<lab>/                               │         │
│  │   ├ data/      ← all lab data                       │         │
│  │   ├ papers/    ← LaTeX + PDFs                       │         │
│  │   ├ skills/    ← agent skills                       │         │
│  │   ├ workflows/ ← slash commands                     │         │
│  │   ├ memory/    ← 4-layer memory                     │         │
│  │   └ audit/     ← per-agent audit logs               │         │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘         │
│                                                                  │
└────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                     │
                     │  (only outbound, only when user
                     │   explicitly invokes a remote skill)
                     ▼
       ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
       │  Allowed external services (opt-in):     │
       │   ├ Anthropic / OpenAI / Google APIs     │
       │   ├ RunPod (for GPU jobs only)           │
       │   ├ HuggingFace (skill-gated)            │
       │   ├ AlphaXiv / arXiv / NASA / etc        │
       │   └ Backblaze B2 (encrypted, optional)   │
       └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The container is one image (`hubify/orchestrator:local`), launched by the desktop app or CLI on first lab create. Lab data lives in volume mounts under `~/.hubify/labs/<lab>/`, NEVER inside the container, so the user owns the bits.

---

## 3. Bootstrap flow

```bash
# Step 1: install Docker (one-time, user prereq)
# (we don't bundle Docker; we check for it and prompt)

# Step 2: create a local lab
hubify lab create my-lab --local
# → checks `docker --version` exists
# → pulls hubify/orchestrator:local image (~250 MB compressed)
# → creates ~/.hubify/labs/my-lab/ with the standard lab template
# → starts the container with the lab volume mounted
# → waits for health check on http://localhost:8080/health
# → prints: "Local lab ready at localhost:8080 · open the desktop app to get started"

# Step 3: switch the desktop app or CLI to talk to the local orchestrator
hubify config set profile local
# → updates ~/.hubify/config.yaml with profile=local
# → next CLI / desktop / web invocation hits localhost:8080

# Step 4 (optional): start in air-gapped mode with no Convex cloud
hubify lab create my-lab --local --no-cloud
# → also runs a local Convex shim (SQLite-backed)
# → no outbound traffic at all unless an explicit remote skill fires
```

The container can be stopped and restarted with `hubify lab pause my-lab` / `hubify lab resume my-lab`. Stopping the container stops the orchestrator (and any in-flight cron jobs queue until resume).

---

## 4. What stays the same vs Fly mode

The user-facing surface is identical:

- **Same web UI**, optionally hosted at `localhost:3000` if running in `--no-cloud` mode
- **Same desktop app** (just points at `localhost:8080`)
- **Same CLI** with all 120 commands
- **Same MCP server** with all 30 tools and 15 resources
- **Same 21 agents** pre-wired (Director · Orchestrator · 4 Leads · 11 Workers + 4 cross-provider reviewers)
- **Same skills + workflows + databases + formats** catalogs
- **Same multi-lab framework** — a user can have 3 cloud labs and 2 local labs side-by-side
- **Same publish-ready loop** (PRD §37) — papers compile in the local container
- **Same Houston Method v2** post-experiment ritual (PRD §13.1)
- **Same lab.toml config schema** with one extra field: `orchestrator.mode = "local" | "fly"`

---

## 5. What changes vs Fly mode

The 7 things that genuinely differ:

### 5.1 No always-on cron
- **Fly mode:** crons fire on the schedule no matter what
- **Local mode:** crons only fire when the orchestrator container is running. The container starts on machine boot via a launchd / systemd hint, but if the laptop is asleep, the cron is queued. Drift is reported in the next standup.
- **Workaround:** Director sees a "missed cron" pill in the briefing card if any cron lapsed > 1 hour past schedule.

### 5.2 No public lab site
- **Fly mode:** every lab gets a free `<lab>.hubify.app` Vercel deployment
- **Local mode:** the public site generator is **disabled by default**. There's no Fly machine to push to Vercel from.
- **Workaround 1:** user can opt-in to a "publish to Vercel manually" flow that runs the static site generator locally and pushes the resulting `dist/` to a user-owned Vercel project. We document this in `vercel-pages` setup guide. Lab data still never leaves the box; only the publish-step output (papers, figures, public claims) goes to Vercel.
- **Workaround 2:** user can run the lab site as `localhost:3001` for personal viewing.

### 5.3 No cross-lab comms with cloud labs
- **Fly mode:** the comm gateway routes between labs (PRD §40.11 Lab Sovereignty Rule applies, reads OK across labs, writes via comm only)
- **Local mode:** a local lab cannot send or receive comms with a cloud lab. The comm queue is local-to-local only.
- **Why:** the Lab Sovereignty Rule + the privacy reason for going local in the first place. We do not want to silently sync local lab metadata to the cloud just to enable a comm.
- **Workaround:** explicit `hubify lab share <local-lab> <cloud-lab>` command flips a flag that allows ONE-WAY READ from cloud to local. The local lab can never push to cloud.

### 5.4 No ntfy phone push
- **Fly mode:** Fly machine pushes to `ntfy.sh` for alerts
- **Local mode:** no Fly machine = no daemon to push from when the laptop is asleep
- **Workaround:** local container pushes ntfy alerts only when running. Missed alerts pile up in the lab inbox and surface in the next session.

### 5.5 Backups must be configured by the user
- **Fly mode:** Backblaze B2 nightly is automatic per `DEPLOYMENT_INFRA_PLAN.md` §2.5
- **Local mode:** B2 backup is **opt-in**. If the user wants offsite backup, they configure a B2 bucket and an encryption key in `lab.toml`. Otherwise the lab is only as durable as the user's local disk + whatever they have set up themselves.
- **Strong recommendation:** the bootstrap flow explicitly prompts the user to configure either B2 OR an external drive backup destination on first lab create. `hubify lab create` refuses to complete without acknowledging this.

### 5.6 Higher local resource use
- **Fly mode:** the orchestrator runs on Fly · the user's laptop is just a thin client
- **Local mode:** the orchestrator container needs ~500 MB RAM idle, ~2 GB under active agent load (multiple Claude Code subprocesses). The MCP server is a separate ~80 MB. Convex local shim is ~150 MB. A typical lab uses ~3 GB resident.
- **Compute view warns** the user when resident > 4 GB · and refuses to start a 3rd local lab if total > 8 GB unless overridden.

### 5.7 Compute provider stays cloud
- **Fly mode:** RunPod for GPU
- **Local mode:** RunPod for GPU **is the same** — local mode doesn't change GPU access. There is no plausible way to give an independent researcher H200-class compute on a laptop.
- **Implication:** any experiment dispatched to RunPod still leaves the box. The local Docker mode protects the orchestrator + lab data + paper manuscripts + chat history, but a GPU job's input data necessarily transits to RunPod. Users who can't tolerate that should stick to CPU-only experiments (which run inside the Docker container on local CPU).

---

## 6. The honest tradeoff table

| Feature | Fly mode | Local mode |
|---|---|---|
| Always-on 24/7 cron | ✅ | ❌ (only when machine is awake) |
| Public `<lab>.hubify.app` site | ✅ free | ⚠️ user-configured manual publish |
| Cross-lab comms with cloud labs | ✅ | ❌ (local-to-local only) |
| ntfy phone push | ✅ | ⚠️ only when running |
| Backblaze B2 backup | ✅ automatic | ⚠️ opt-in user-configured |
| Resource cost | $2-5/lab/month Fly | $0/month, but uses local RAM + CPU |
| Privacy boundary | Lab data on Fly + Convex cloud | **Lab data never leaves the box** (except explicit GPU dispatch) |
| Air-gapped capable | ❌ | ✅ with `--no-cloud` flag |
| Setup complexity | One CLI command | Docker prereq + one CLI command |
| Multi-machine sync | ✅ via cloud | ❌ (local lab is tied to one machine; user must manually rsync to move) |

---

## 7. Migration: cloud → local and local → cloud

Users can move a lab in either direction.

### 7.1 Cloud → local

```bash
hubify lab migrate my-lab --to local
# → tar + encrypted-download from B2 + rehydrate into ~/.hubify/labs/my-lab/
# → starts the local container
# → updates lab.toml: orchestrator.mode = "local"
# → keeps the cloud Convex deployment alive for 7 days as a rollback safety net
# → after 7 days, prompts user to confirm deletion of the cloud copy
```

### 7.2 Local → cloud

```bash
hubify lab migrate my-lab --to fly
# → checks B2 backup is current
# → uploads the local lab to a fresh Fly machine + Convex deployment
# → updates lab.toml: orchestrator.mode = "fly"
# → keeps the local container alive for 7 days as a rollback safety net
```

Both directions preserve all 4 memory layers, all chats, all papers, all audit logs.

---

## 8. Image structure

```
hubify/orchestrator:local
├── /app/                          # node + python runtime, claude-code binary
├── /usr/local/bin/hubify          # CLI binary (so the container can self-invoke)
├── /var/hubify/                   # writable working directory (volume mount)
│   └── (labs mounted here per-launch)
└── /etc/hubify/                   # default config templates
```

Image is published at `ghcr.io/hubify-labs/orchestrator:local-<version>` per the standard CI/CD pipeline (DEPLOYMENT_INFRA_PLAN §2.7). Pinned to a stable version per lab via `lab.toml` so a user upgrading hubify doesn't surprise-break a frozen lab.

---

## 9. Security

- The container runs as a non-root user (`hubify:hubify` uid 1000)
- No port binding except `localhost:8080` (orchestrator API) and `localhost:3000` (web UI in `--no-cloud` mode) — never `0.0.0.0`
- Lab volume mounts are mode 0700 owned by the launching user
- Secrets (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` etc) are passed via env vars at container start, not baked into the image
- In `--no-cloud` mode, the container is started with `--network none` for the orchestrator process and a tightly-scoped `--network bridge` only when an explicit outbound skill fires (managed by an inner proxy)
- All writes inside the container are append-only audit-logged to `audit/local-mode.jsonl`

---

## 10. Open questions

1. **Default to local or cloud?** Right now the default is Fly mode. Should privacy-sensitive labs (bio + clinical) auto-detect their domain and prompt for local mode? **Proposed default:** no auto-detection — make the choice explicit at lab create time, but show the tradeoff table prominently in the create wizard.
2. **Windows + WSL2 support?** Local Docker mode "works" on Windows via Docker Desktop + WSL2 but the desktop app is macOS-only at v1 per `DESKTOP_APP_SPEC.md`. Should we ship Windows support for local mode at v1, or punt to v1.1? **Proposed default:** v1.1 — local mode on Windows requires Windows desktop app, which is its own whole spec.
3. **Convex local shim** — building a SQLite-backed Convex shim is real work (the Convex API surface is large). Should we ship `--no-cloud` mode at v1 or punt? **Proposed default:** ship `--local` (with cloud Convex) at v1, ship `--local --no-cloud` at v1.1. The privacy story still works for v1 because the lab DATA never goes to Convex — only the lab metadata + chat history. Users with ironclad air-gap requirements wait for v1.1.
4. **GPU dispatch from local mode** — should we expose a "local GPU only" toggle that refuses RunPod dispatch? **Proposed default:** yes, ship the toggle. Default OFF (RunPod allowed). Users who flip it ON acknowledge they lose access to H200-class compute.
